conventions.convention: The Lie algebra is complex of type A, W=S_n, and λ is dominant regular integral. The dot action is w·λ=w(λ+ρ)−ρ; e labels the dominant weight and w₀ labels the antidominant weight.

Δ(y·λ)=M(y·λ), and (P(w·λ):Δ(y·λ))=[M(y·λ):L(w·λ)]. Nonzero multiplicity requires y≤w in Bruhat order. The text asserts only the two stated Bruhat/dominance implications, not an isomorphism of these orders.

V has left coinvariant-module values, right reduction is B⊗_S C, and V(P(w·λ))≅bar B_{w⁻¹}. Polynomial graph label x corresponds to Δ(x⁻¹·λ). Standard-support ranks are measured before origin reduction.

q=v⁻² and p_{y,w}=v^{ℓ(w)−ℓ(y)}P_{y,w}(v⁻²). The standard Hecke element H_s=vT_s is distinct from the Soergel supplier's generator H_i=v(T_i+1)=H_s+v. The normalized standard layer is Δ_x(d)=R_x(d−ℓ(x)), contributing v^d.

Q′=(q′_{x,w}) is the inverse of the normalized coefficient matrix (p_{x,w}). Simple characters use row w: [L(w·λ)]=Σ_{x≥w}q′_{w,x}(1)[M(x·λ)]. These are weighted incidence-inverse coefficients; ordinary Bruhat Möbius values apply when every comparable-pair KL value in the interval is 1.
The proved multiplicity and character results assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the category-O prerequisites.
The polynomial Soergel grading is auxiliary. These items establish ordinary multiplicities at q=1 and do not construct a category-O grading, Koszul structure, or Ext refinement.

Regular-to-regular translation uses E=L(ν), with ν the dominant member of W(μ−λ), and reverse translation uses E*. It preserves dot-orbit labels and Grothendieck identities; formal weight characters of different blocks need not coincide.

load_bearing.statement: Fix a complex type-A Lie algebra and a dominant regular integral λ. Standards, simples and projectives have dot-orbit labels; BGG reciprocity uses (P(w·λ):Δ(y·λ))=[M(y·λ):L(w·λ)], and the Soergel dictionary uses inverse labels w⁻¹ with pre-reduction polynomial support ranks.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. In a regular integral type-A block, for all y,w∈W, (P(w·λ):Δ(y·λ))=Σ_d r_{y⁻¹,d}(B_{w⁻¹}), where these are normalized polynomial standard-support multiplicities before reduction.
Assume the Axiom of Choice. In a regular integral type-A block O_λ, for all y,w∈W, (P(w·λ):Δ(y·λ))=P_{y,w}(1); the multiplicity is the total value at one and vanishes unless y≤w.
Assume the Axiom of Choice. In a regular integral type-A block O_λ, for all y,w∈W, [M(y·λ):L(w·λ)]=(P(w·λ):Δ(y·λ))=P_{y,w}(1), with vanishing unless y≤w.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. In a regular integral type-A block O_λ, for every w∈W, [L(w·λ)]=Σ_x q′_{w,x}(1)[M(x·λ)], equivalently ch L(w·λ)=Σ_x q′_{w,x}(1)ch M(x·λ), supported on x≥w, where Q′=(p_{x,w})⁻¹.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For dominant regular integral λ,μ of the same complex type-A Lie algebra and positive system, the specified tensor/block-projection translations using E=L(ν) and E*, with ν the dominant member of W(μ−λ), are exact mutually inverse equivalences preserving labelled standards, simples and projective covers, multiplicities and the inverse-KL Grothendieck identity.

concerns.concern: The opening says 'dominant regular integral weight λ, i.e.' and then specifies only integrality and nonzero root pairings of λ+ρ. That parenthetical omits dominance; for example −2ρ satisfies the listed conditions. The surrounding dominant-weight requirement and cited block definition fix the intended domain, so this is a wording correction rather than a change to the mathematics.

Fact F6 contains the malformed expression 'End(M)=M↦ scalars'. The required and subsequently used assertion is End(M)=C·id_M for every Verma module, which follows from the cited dimension bound and the nonzero identity.

alerts.finding: Proof 1.1 says: 'The restrictions of any two maps f,g:M(μ)→M(λ) are proportional, say f|_S=cg|_S.' This oriented equality need not exist when g=0 and f≠0; injectivity makes f|_S≠0. The dimension claim remains sound: handle the zero Hom space separately and fix a nonzero g before comparing arbitrary f. This is an immediate proof repair, not a false theorem.

seams_checked.note: Read the supplier block definition, projective/Soergel dictionary and standard-rank comparison. The consumer preserves dominant labels, P(w·λ)↦bar B_{w⁻¹}, graph-label inversion, Choice, type-A scope and ranks before reduction. Its lemma specializes the general comparison to one indecomposable projective. It does not claim separated supports after reduction or a grading on category O.

Read the singular and parabolic multiplicity consumers. Singular F3/1.2 explicitly rebases the antidominant regular parameter to λ_dom and uses P_{yw₀,ww₀}(1). Parabolic F4/2.1 uses P_{uy,x}(1) only for the dominant regular ambient block; F5 cites the actual label-preserving regular translations. Both preserve type-A and regularity qualifications. The dominant-label normalization also agrees, after rebasing the shifted antidominant parameter and conjugating indices by w₀, with [Yee, Introduction, pp. 1–2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1207.3423).
